title.narrative: Study agrologistics in the Colombian Caribbean

description.narrative: The agricultural potential of Colombia is, without a doubt, enormous. However, it is not yet fully exploited. Meanwhile, Colombian cities steadily grow both in size and population, demanding agricultural production of higher quality and quantity. With this, comes to need for an efficient set of infrastructure and logistics operations, both for domestic and international trade. This study aimed to analyse and present the current situation of the agro-logistics sector in the five departments of Atla´ntico, Boli´var, Cesar, La Guajira and Magdalena. These five departments host three of the four main ports for Colombia, playing a crucial role in the import and export operations of the country. In addition, they are home to large production of banana and oil palm. The project provides a comprehensive understanding of the current state of the art and bottlenecks of the agro-logistic chains in the focus regions . In addition, the regions are described in their environmental and geographical aspects, on top of being linked to the different logistics systems available in the region (and country). Building on the results of the first part of the study, The results of this project contribute to the identification of integrated value chain solutions and bussines cases that will improve the logistics for perishable goods and reduce food loss and waste, improve incomes of producers and further exploit the export potential of the Caribbean region and the country. In doing so, the project identified several business opportunities for involvement of the knowledge and private sector of the Netherlands and Colombia. The study was performed by Resilience BV, with the support of the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bogotá.

The project provides a comprehensive understanding of the current state of the art and bottlenecks of the agro-logistic chains along multi-modal transport in the Caribbean region of Colombia. The results of this project contribute to the identification of integrated value chain solutions and business cases that will improve the logistics for perishable goods and reduce food loss and waste, improve incomes of producers and further exploit the export potential of the Caribbean region and the country. In doing so, the project also identifies opportunities for involvement of the knowledge and private sector of the Netherlands and Colombia. The project has a positive impact on:SDG 8: inclusive and sustainable economic growth; andSDG 2: food nutrition and security
